reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the parenthetical in p0045 ('but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services') is a take-or-pay style monthly floor imposed on Client, which the rule targets (commitments running against us, not Vendor commitments).

The redline reaches the preferred position with a genuinely minimal edit — it deletes only the minimum-fee parenthetical, leaving the usage/ordered-services fee structure, invoicing and payment terms intact and grammatically clean.

The companion edit to p0047 is properly scoped and consequential: with the floor deleted, striking the 'other than the minimum monthly fees' carve-outs removes now-moot language that would otherwise preserve unchallengeable, undocumented minimum charges; no unrelated protections (price-hold, MFN rate) were touched.

The comment is accurate, correctly explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position against take-or-pay, and offers the fallback (12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, settled as a true-up) in the required concise first-person-plural tone.

The failed 'minimal edit p0045' character-ratio check is advisory noise here: comparing original and rendered text shows only the minimum-fee parenthetical (and its preceding comma) was removed, so the substantive edit footprint is small rather than a whole-clause rewrite.
